[{"content":"You are a teaching assistant analyzing a teacher's audio transcript about student observations.

Your task:
1. Identify which students are mentioned in the transcript
2. Match each mentioned name to the student roster below (handle phonetic/partial matches)
3. Extract the date if mentioned (format YYYY-MM-DD), otherwise leave empty
4. Write a summary per student capturing what the teacher said about them
   - Clean up speech artifacts (false starts, filler words, repetitions) into clear sentences
   - Preserve the teacher's voice, tone, and specific observations — do NOT add details or opinions not present in the transcript
   - Keep the teacher's vocabulary and perspective (first person if they used it)
   - Combine multiple mentions of the same student into a cohesive note

Student Roster:
- Emma Torres (class_name Class A)
- Ryan Mitchell (class_name Class A)
- Lila Patel (class_name Class A)

Rules:
- Match mentioned names against the roster even if pronunciation differs slightly
- Some roster entries include "(aka ...)" aliases — if a teacher uses an alias, match it to the canonical name and return the canonical name in the "name" field
- Set confidence 0.0-1.0 for each match. Use >= 0.7 for confident matches.
- If confidence < 0.7, include up to 3 closest roster matches in "candidates"
- A student is "individually mentioned" ONLY if the teacher uses their name (or a recognizable nickname/variant of their name). Generic group references like "everyone", "all students", "the class" do NOT count as individual mentions.
- Do NOT create entries for students who are never individually mentioned by name. If a student is only covered by group-level observations (e.g. "the class was loud") but never called out by name, they must NOT appear in the output.
- For students who ARE individually mentioned by name, their quoted_text MUST include BOTH their individual observations AND any group-level observations from the same transcript/class. This applies to EVERY individually-mentioned student in that class, regardless of where the group observation appears in the transcript (beginning, middle, or end) or which students were named immediately before/after it. Do not attach group observations only to the students mentioned closest to them — propagate them to all named students in the class.
  Example: Transcript says "Alice did great. Bob was quiet. The whole class struggled with fractions." → BOTH Alice's and Bob's quoted_text must include the fractions observation, not just Bob's.
- If the transcript contains group references like "everyone", "all students", or "the class", apply those observations only to students in the class being discussed, not to ALL classes. Use context clues (class name mentions, prior student mentions) to determine which class is meant.
- For multi-student transcripts, produce a separate entry per student with relevant passages
- If a mentioned student cannot be matched to any roster entry, do not include them in the output
- If no students are clearly mentioned, return an empty students array
- The "class_name" field for each student MUST exactly match one of the class names from the roster above. Do not invent or abbreviate class names.
- IMPORTANT: Clean up speech into readable sentences, but do NOT invent observations or editorialize. Stay faithful to what the teacher actually said.

Assessment (Participation / Motivation): Good

Comment:

Chloé generally comes to class in a cheerful mood, though her energy levels vary—she was notably tired on one occasion. She shows willingness to participate, especially in hands-on activities like dressing Emma and the "what's missing" game, which she enjoyed. While she sometimes holds back when unsure, such as with colours and clothing vocabulary, she engages well once guided. Chloé is cooperative with her classmates, though she occasionally requires reminders to focus, particularly when repeating questions or seeking reassurance about tasks she already understands. Her enthusiasm for new elements, like the story tattoo activity, is evident, and she responds positively to redirection when distracted.

Learning process

Assessment (Learning process): Satisfactory

Comment:

Chloé’s English knowledge is developing, though unevenly across areas. She has strengths in:

  • Using complete structures for personal information (e.g., stating her age and gender).
  • Understanding and pairing concepts like clean/dirty and dry/wet, as well as body parts with actions (e.g., placing tattoos correctly).

Assessment (Behaviour): Good

Comment:

Chloé is a playful and sociable student who generally integrates well with her peers. Kids&Us.

Objectives and content of the Emma course, 3rd term

Term report (3rd term)

Data

  • Name: Chloé
  • Class: Emma Saturday

Participation/Motivation

Assessment (Participation / Motivation): Good

Comment:

Chloé generally comes to class in a cheerful mood, though her energy levels vary—she was notably tired on one occasion. She shows willingness to participate, especially in hands-on activities like dressing Emma and the "what's missing" game, which she enjoyed. While she sometimes holds back when unsure, such as with colours and clothing vocabulary, she engages well once guided. Chloé is cooperative with her classmates, though she occasionally requires reminders to focus, particularly when repeating questions or seeking reassurance about tasks she already understands. Her enthusiasm for new elements, like the story tattoo activity, is evident, and she responds positively to redirection when distracted.

Learning process

Assessment (Learning process): Satisfactory

Comment:

Chloé’s English knowledge is developing, though unevenly across areas. She has strengths in:

  • Using complete structures for personal information (e.g., stating her age and gender).
  • Understanding and pairing concepts like clean/dirty and dry/wet, as well as body parts with actions (e.g., placing tattoos correctly).
  • Following worksheet activities and counting with accuracy.
  • Repeating new vocabulary and structures when prompted, showing progress in retention.

Her weaknesses include:

  • Limited recall of colours and clothing vocabulary, often requiring teacher support to identify or pair items.
  • Difficulty internalising story details independently—she needed significant help to retell the story initially, though her comprehension improved later.
  • Over-reliance on repetition of questions ("quoi quoi quoi") during instructions, indicating gaps in listening confidence.

Plan for improvement: Chloé would benefit from:

  • Targeted practice with colours and clothing vocabulary through games or flashcards to reinforce recognition.
  • Encouragement to listen attentively to instructions before seeking clarification, building her autonomy.
  • Storytelling exercises to strengthen her ability to sequence and retell narratives independently.
The school will continue to provide structured support during these activities to help her consolidate these skills.

Behaviour

Assessment (Behaviour): Good

Comment:

Chloé is a playful and sociable student who generally integrates well with her peers. Chloé handles materials carefully and shares with her peers when prompted.

Chloé has shown growth in her participation and learning this term, particularly in her ability to follow structured activities and use language in context. Her enthusiasm for interactive tasks, like dressing Emma and body-part games, highlights her potential to thrive with hands-on learning. While she still needs support to internalise vocabulary and listen independently, her willingness to engage and improve is commendable. With continued practice—especially in areas like colours, clothing, and storytelling—she will build greater confidence. Assessment (Participation / Motivation): Very good

Comment:
Chloé usually comes to class in a good mood and is generally willing to take part in the activities proposed. At the beginning of some sessions, she could be a little loud or repeatedly ask for confirmation, but she usually settles well when given clear guidance. Chloé is cooperative with the teacher and with her classmates, and she especially enjoys hands-on activities such as worksheet work, bingo, cards and dressing Emma.

Learning process

Assessment (Learning process): Satisfactory

Comment:
Chloé's English knowledge is satisfactory. She can repeat the new structures well and often understands the language being worked on in class. This term, she worked on colours, clothes, body parts, actions, rooms and places, as well as the concepts of clean/dirty and dry/wet. She can usually tell her age and gender and, on several occasions, used the complete structure correctly. She was also able to pair actions with the correct rooms and take part in the story-time activities. However, she still needs more practice with some vocabulary items, especially clothes and colours, and she sometimes needs the teacher's help to remember or apply the full structure. With more regular revision, she will continue to gain confidence and accuracy.

Behaviour

Assessment (Behaviour): Good

Comment:
Chloé is a lively and generally well-integrated student. She can be a little distracted or impatient at times, especially when she is tired or when the group is especially active, but she responds well to reminders and class management strategies. Once the rules are clear, she behaves appropriately and stays focused on the task. She usually treats the material carefully and works well with the rest of the group. Her attitude in class is positive and she is able to adapt well to the pace of the lesson.

Final comment

Throughout the term, Chloé has shown a positive attitude towards the classroom routines and has taken part well in the activities. She is able to understand and repeat a good part of the language worked on in class, and she is becoming more confident when using complete structures. She still needs to keep reinforcing some vocabulary, especially clothes and colours, but she is making good progress. Well done, Chloé! It is recommended to keep listening to the audio tracks and revising the vocabulary at home in order to consolidate the language learnt during the term.

Motivation and Participation

Chloé came to class in a very good mood. At the beginning of the lesson, the group was a bit loud, but once the traffic light was put in place, she participated super well. She was open to the new activities, liked the new story tattoo and was excited to hear more. Behaviour

On one day, she was quite distracted and tired. She also needed to pay attention during workshop instructions, as she kept asking “quoi quoi quoi” until she stopped. The class was playful and loud at times, but it could calm down when reminded.

Learning

Chloé could repeat the new vocabulary words and the new structures, and she could pair up the correct actions in the correct rooms. She understood the clean and dirty concept, as well as dry and wet, and she could understand the “Emma is wearing...” activity. She could tell her age and gender, almost always using the complete structure, and she could pair Emma’s dirty and clean body parts, although she sometimes needed reminders to use the full structure. She did very well in the worksheet activity, could count very well, and could ask for the counters while understanding the corresponding colour and clothing item on her bingo card.

Her knowledge was less secure with colours, clothes and clothing items: she did not know the colours or the clothes, and she did not really master the clothing items vocabulary. On one occasion, she did not know the story at all and needed help to tell it, while on another day she knew the story very well. We will continue working on these areas, with support on vocabulary cards and complete structures.

Motivation and Participation

Assessment (Motivation / Participation): Good

Comment:

Mila often arrives in class in a happy mood and shows a willingness to learn, particularly when she is familiar with the material. She actively participates in activities she enjoys, such as the Present for Me game, Family Bingo, and the Dice Game, where she demonstrates enthusiasm and engagement. Mila is quick to combine moods and actions, as well as weather and clothing vocabulary, showing her ability to apply what she has learned.

However, her motivation fluctuates when things do not go her way. She occasionally withdraws from participation—such as during the True or False activity and the Dice Game—when she feels frustrated, like when she was not allowed to keep the blu-tack. Despite this, she recovers well and rejoins activities, as seen when she initially resisted routines due to a headache but later participated fully. Her knowledge of structures and vocabulary is strong, and she often repeats them accurately, which helps her contribute positively to group tasks.

Behaviour

Assessment (Behaviour): Satisfactory

Comment:

Mila generally interacts well with the group, especially during activities she finds engaging. She shows a good understanding of classroom expectations and can follow instructions, such as during the weather routines and action activities. However, her behaviour can be inconsistent when faced with challenges. For example, she became upset during story time when she couldn’t see the Big Book but did not take initiative to adjust her position. She also laid down and turned her back during the story out of frustration.

While Mila is cooperative and often eager to help—such as when the class handed out materials—she sometimes struggles with emotional regulation. Her mood can affect her focus, particularly toward the end of longer activities when the group grows restless. With gentle reminders, she refocuses and re-engages, demonstrating her ability to recover and participate positively.

Learning

Assessment (Learning process): Good

Comment:

Mila has shown solid progress in her understanding of vocabulary and structures. She knows the story well and can retell most of it with minimal support, demonstrating strong comprehension. Her ability to pair weather items with clothing and describe what she is wearing indicates she is applying new language effectively. She also excels in color vocabulary, including newer terms like white and black, and performs worksheet activities with accuracy.

Areas for improvement include the phrases taking off and putting on, where she still requires assistance. Additionally, her participation in less preferred activities, such as the True or False game, can be hesitant. To build consistency, Mila would benefit from practising these structures in varied contexts and developing strategies to manage frustration when tasks feel challenging. Her strong foundation and enthusiasm suggest she has great potential to refine these skills further.

Final comment

Mila has made notable progress this term, particularly in her vocabulary retention and ability to apply structures in activities. Her enthusiasm for games and storytelling is a strength, and she often inspires her peers with her knowledge. While her participation and behaviour can vary based on her mood, she shows resilience and a willingness to re-engage when guided. With continued practice—especially in areas like clothing routines and emotional regulation—Mila is well on her way to even greater confidence and success. Keep up the good work, Mila!

Kids&Us.

Objectives and content of the Oliver course, 3rd term

Term report (3rd term)

Data

  • Name: Mila
  • Class: Oliver Thursday

Motivation and Participation

Assessment (Motivation / Participation): Good

Comment:

Mila often arrives in class in a happy mood and shows a willingness to learn, particularly when she is familiar with the material. She actively participates in activities she enjoys, such as the Present for Me game, Family Bingo, and the Dice Game, where she demonstrates enthusiasm and engagement. Mila is quick to combine moods and actions, as well as weather and clothing vocabulary, showing her ability to apply what she has learned.

However, her motivation fluctuates when things do not go her way. She occasionally withdraws from participation—such as during the True or False activity and the Dice Game—when she feels frustrated, like when she was not allowed to keep the blu-tack. Despite this, she recovers well and rejoins activities, as seen when she initially resisted routines due to a headache but later participated fully. Her knowledge of structures and vocabulary is strong, and she often repeats them accurately, which helps her contribute positively to group tasks.

Behaviour

Assessment (Behaviour): Satisfactory

Comment:

Mila generally interacts well with the group, especially during activities she finds engaging. She shows a good understanding of classroom expectations and can follow instructions, such as during the weather routines and action activities. However, her behaviour can be inconsistent when faced with challenges. For example, she became upset during story time when she couldn’t see the Big Book but did not take initiative to adjust her position. She also laid down and turned her back during the story out of frustration.

While Mila is cooperative and often eager to help—such as when the class handed out materials—she sometimes struggles with emotional regulation. Her mood can affect her focus, particularly toward the end of longer activities when the group grows restless. With gentle reminders, she refocuses and re-engages, demonstrating her ability to recover and participate positively.

Learning

Assessment (Learning process): Good

Comment:

Mila has shown solid progress in her understanding of vocabulary and structures. She knows the story well and can retell most of it with minimal support, demonstrating strong comprehension. Her ability to pair weather items with clothing and describe what she is wearing indicates she is applying new language effectively. She also excels in color vocabulary, including newer terms like white and black, and performs worksheet activities with accuracy.

Areas for improvement include the phrases taking off and putting on, where she still requires assistance. Additionally, her participation in less preferred activities, such as the True or False game, can be hesitant. To build consistency, Mila would benefit from practising these structures in varied contexts and developing strategies to manage frustration when tasks feel challenging. Her strong foundation and enthusiasm suggest she has great potential to refine these skills further.

Final comment

Mila has made notable progress this term, particularly in her vocabulary retention and ability to apply structures in activities. Her enthusiasm for games and storytelling is a strength, and she often inspires her peers with her knowledge. While her participation and behaviour can vary based on her mood, she shows resilience and a willingness to re-engage when guided. With continued practice—especially in areas like clothing routines and emotional regulation—Mila is well on her way to even greater confidence and success. Keep up the good work, Mila!

Name: Mila
Class: Oliver Thursday

Participation/Motivation

Assessment (Participation / Motivation): Good

Comment:
Mila generally shows a happy and willing attitude in class, particularly when activities align with her interests. She participates eagerly in action-based tasks and enjoys activities like A present for me, Dice Game, and Family Bingo. However, her motivation sometimes wanes when she does not get her way, such as when she was upset about not seeing the Big Book or not being allowed to keep the blu-tack. She initially holds back in new or challenging situations, like the stamp activity, but often recovers and engages once she feels more comfortable. Her willingness to help with materials and her ability to combine moods, actions, and vocabulary demonstrate her growing confidence in familiar tasks.

Learning process

Assessment (Learning process): Good

Comment:
Mila has a strong grasp of the vocabulary, structures, songs, and gestures covered in class. She can retell parts of the story with minimal help and pairs weather realia items with the correct sentences effectively. Her understanding of color vocabulary, including black and white, is solid, and she applies it well in activities. She also demonstrates proficiency in combining weather and clothing items. However, she occasionally needs support with specific phrases, such as "taking off" and "putting on" during weather routines. With continued practice, she will further internalize these structures.

Behaviour

Assessment (Behaviour): Satisfactory

Comment:
Mila is usually cooperative and integrates well with the group, especially during activities she enjoys. However, she sometimes struggles with emotional regulation, such as laying down, turning her back, or refusing to participate when frustrated. Her mood can affect her focus, as seen when she initially disengaged due to a headache or dissatisfaction. The class as a whole also showed restlessness by the end of longer activities, which occasionally impacted her engagement. With gentle reminders and encouragement, she typically recovers and contributes positively to the group dynamic.

Final comment

Mila has shown good progress this term, particularly in her use of vocabulary and structures. Her enthusiasm for interactive activities is a strength, and she demonstrates a solid understanding of the material when engaged. To build on this, she would benefit from practising emotional regulation strategies to help her stay focused even when faced with minor setbacks. With continued encouragement, she will further develop her confidence and participation in all class activities.

Term report (3rd term)

Data

Name: Mila
Class: Oliver Thursday

Participation/Motivation

Assessment (Participation / Motivation): Good

Comment:
Mila generally shows a happy and willing attitude in class, particularly when activities align with her interests. She participates eagerly in action-based tasks and enjoys activities like A present for me, Dice Game, and Family Bingo. However, her motivation sometimes wanes when she does not get her way, such as when she was upset about not seeing the Big Book or not being allowed to keep the blu-tack. She initially holds back in new or challenging situations, like the stamp activity, but often recovers and engages once she feels more comfortable. Her willingness to help with materials and her ability to combine moods, actions, and vocabulary demonstrate her growing confidence in familiar tasks.

Learning process

Assessment (Learning process): Good

Comment:
Mila has a strong grasp of the vocabulary, structures, songs, and gestures covered in class. She can retell parts of the story with minimal help and pairs weather realia items with the correct sentences effectively. Her understanding of color vocabulary, including black and white, is solid, and she applies it well in activities. She also demonstrates proficiency in combining weather and clothing items. However, she occasionally needs support with specific phrases, such as "taking off" and "putting on" during weather routines. With continued practice, she will further internalize these structures.

Behaviour

Assessment (Behaviour): Satisfactory

Comment:
Mila is usually cooperative and integrates well with the group, especially during activities she enjoys. However, she sometimes struggles with emotional regulation, such as laying down, turning her back, or refusing to participate when frustrated. Her mood can affect her focus, as seen when she initially disengaged due to a headache or dissatisfaction. The class as a whole also showed restlessness by the end of longer activities, which occasionally impacted her engagement. With gentle reminders and encouragement, she typically recovers and contributes positively to the group dynamic.

Final comment

Mila has shown good progress this term, particularly in her use of vocabulary and structures. Her enthusiasm for interactive activities is a strength, and she demonstrates a solid understanding of the material when engaged. To build on this, she would benefit from practising emotional regulation strategies to help her stay focused even when faced with minor setbacks. With continued encouragement, she will further develop her confidence and participation in all class activities.

Data

  • Name: Mila
  • Class: Oliver Thursday

Motivation and Participation

Mila generally comes to class in a very happy mood and shows a clear willingness to take part in the activities. She knows some of the vocabulary and can repeat the structures, and she also understands and uses the language being worked on during class tasks. Mila participates especially well in activities she enjoys, such as the action activity and the present activity, and she was happy to help hand out the material. At times, though, her participation decreases when she does not get her way or feels upset. On one occasion she only listened at first, did not join in the routines straight away, and later refused to take part in the True or False activity and the Dice Game. She also needed help with the words used for “taking off” and “putting on” during the weather routines.

Behaviour

Mila is usually well integrated in the group and can be cooperative, especially during shared classroom moments. However, when she is unhappy, she tends to close up and can react strongly. She became upset because she could not see the Big Book during story time and did not move to improve her view. She laid down a few times, was asked to sit, and turned her back during the whole story because she was angry. On another day she said she had a headache, and this affected her involvement at the beginning of the lesson. The group needed to move around a lot, and they seemed to become bored by the end of the story.

Learning

Mila has shown that she already knows much of the vocabulary, structures, songs, gestures and story work covered in class. She can combine the mood and the actions very well, knows the phrase that matches her weather card, and can repeat the structures confidently. She also told the story with almost no help and, at another point, could already tell part of it and repeat the rest. Her main difficulty is with the “taking off” and “putting on” words in the weather routines. We will continue supporting her in practising these expressions so that she can feel more secure using them and keep building confidence in class.

Kids&Us.

Objectives and content of the Oliver course, 3rd term

Term report (3rd term)

Data

  • Name: Camille
  • Class: Oliver-Group 2 Saturday

Participation/Motivation

Assessment (Participation / Motivation): Good

Comment:

Camille demonstrates a positive and engaged attitude in class, particularly during interactive activities. She shows enthusiasm for games like A Present for Me, Family Bingo, and the Dice Game, where her participation is notably active. While she occasionally becomes playful with peers—such as with Zoé—she remains attentive overall and willingly joins in group tasks. Her willingness to repeat after the teacher and her enjoyment of new routines, like the weather and mood miming, reflect her openness to learning. Though she sometimes hesitates, encouragement helps her regain confidence, ensuring she stays motivated and involved in classroom activities.

Learning process

Assessment (Learning process): Good

Comment:

Camille has shown solid progress in vocabulary retention, particularly with colors, clothing items, and some prepositions. She understands story elements well, recalling parts of the narrative and completing worksheet activities about Oliver and Baby’s abilities with a clear grasp of the material. While she occasionally requires reminders for correct sentence structures, her memorisation of vocabulary is evident, and she applies it effectively in activities like Who’s Missing. Her ability to quickly adapt to new routines, such as describing physical appearance before guessing characters, highlights her growing comprehension. Continued practice in forming questions and structuring sentences will further strengthen her language skills.

Behaviour

Assessment (Behaviour): Good

Comment:

Camille generally behaves well in the classroom, contributing to a positive group dynamic. She interacts playfully with classmates, though at times—such as when jokingly hiding materials—she needs gentle reminders to follow instructions promptly. Her attentiveness is commendable, especially during storytelling and new activities, where she listens carefully and responds eagerly. While she may show occasional hesitation, her overall demeanor is cooperative and kind. Her enjoyment of collaborative games and routines helps maintain a pleasant atmosphere in the group.

Final comment

____________________________________________________________

Camille has had a productive term, displaying enthusiasm for learning and a strong ability to engage with both familiar and new material. Her vocabulary retention and participation in interactive activities are notable strengths, though she would benefit from further practice in sentence construction and independent questioning. With her positive attitude and willingness to participate, Camille is well-positioned to continue her progress. Encouraging her to build confidence in speaking and reinforcing routines over the summer will help her start the next term with even greater assurance.

Term report (3rd term)

Data

  • Name: Camille
  • Teacher: Thérèse Garnier
  • Level: Oliver-Group 2 Saturday 2025/2026
  • Absences: 0
  • Frequency of use (audio): Pass

Participation/Motivation

Assessment (Participation / Motivation): Very good

Comment:
Camille comes into class with a calm and positive attitude, and she shows a pleasant willingness to take part in the different activities proposed. She is generally attentive and open to new tasks, enjoying the story work, the worksheet activities and games such as Present for me, Who’s Missing and the Dice Game. Camille participates well when she feels comfortable, and she shows interest in the language being worked on, especially when she can recall vocabulary and repeat what she has learned. At times she can be a little more hesitant, but with encouragement she responds well and continues to engage positively with the group.

Learning process

Assessment (Learning process): Good

Comment:
Camille has shown a good understanding of the story and the language structures worked on this term. She can remember vocabulary words very well, especially colours, clothing items and some prepositions, and she also demonstrated understanding in activities about what Oliver and Baby could or could not do. She was able to recite parts of the story and to repeat when asked, showing that she is memorising the language and building her confidence. She sometimes needs help to recall the correct structures, particularly when asking questions or using the new language independently, but she shows real understanding and is making steady progress. Continued practice will help her become more secure and more confident when using the structures spontaneously.

Behaviour

Assessment (Behaviour): Very good

Comment:
Camille has a peaceful, easy-going and attentive manner in class. She is generally well integrated within the group and her calm presence helps create a positive atmosphere. She is usually focused and listens carefully, showing a good level of concentration during activities. On occasion she can be a little playful with the materials or slightly distracted with a classmate, but this does not affect her overall behaviour, which remains very good. Camille responds well to guidance, follows the classroom routine and shows a kind and cooperative attitude towards both the teacher and her peers.

Marks

Oral Test Mark: 8.10  Good. Camille can understand the question and answers either with a single word or with a structure which is only partially correct.

Final comment

____________________________________________________________
Camille has had a positive term and has shown good understanding of the story content and vocabulary worked on in class. Her calm and attentive nature, together with her willingness to participate, have contributed well to the group. She is progressing nicely and, with continued practice and confidence, she will keep developing her language skills next term.

Data

  • Name: Camille
  • Class: Oliver-Group 2 Saturday

Motivation and Participation

Camille was attentive overall and showed a positive attitude towards the activities carried out in class. She loved the Present for me activity and really enjoyed the new story, listening happily and quickly engaging with the routines. She was also very happy to repeat when asked. At times, she was a bit less confident and more hesitant, but she continued to take part with encouragement.

Camille participated well in the worksheet activity and in the activities about what Oliver and Baby could or could not do. She could recite parts of the story, and she showed a real understanding and a certain memorisation of the vocabulary. She also enjoyed activities such as Who’s missing, Family Bingo and the Dice Game. She needed help to remember the correct structures in a lot of the activities, but she kept trying and remained involved. At times, she was not always giving the material back directly when asked and was hiding it jokingly.

Behaviour

Camille was very attentive, and we were really proud of her behaviour. She was a bit distracting with Zoé at times, but it was alright. The group got bored by the end of the story, although Camille was happy to listen to it and seemed to enjoy it. She quickly understood the new weather and action miming routine, as well as the new mood routine with “he’s smiling because he’s happy”.

Learning

Camille knew parts of the story and could recite it partially. She understood the worksheet activity very well and could do the worksheet about what Oliver and Baby could or couldn’t do very well. She could remember the vocabulary words very well, tell the colours and the clothing items very well, and remember some prepositions. Her understanding and memorisation of the vocabulary are strengths.

Camille still needs support to use the correct structures in a lot of the activities, and she is still learning to ask questions about a person’s physical appearance before asking who it is; this is a work in progress. We will continue to encourage her to use the correct structures and to keep working on this question form so that she can gain more confidence and independence.

Assessment (Participation / Motivation): Good

Camille demonstrates a positive attitude towards classroom activities, showing enthusiasm during engaging tasks such as the "Present for me" activity, the "Who’s missing" game, and the Dice Game. She willingly participates in group activities and displays a keen interest in new routines, including the weather and action miming exercises. While she occasionally requires reminders to maintain focus, her overall cooperation with peers and the teacher reflects a constructive approach to learning.

Camille generally integrates well within the group, participating positively in collaborative activities such as the worksheet tasks and group games. She maintains a cheerful demeanor and interacts kindly with her peers. She actively engages with the material, particularly during activities like the worksheet tasks and storytelling exercises. While she occasionally requires support to apply the correct structures, her ability to memorize and recall information is commendable. To further enhance her learning, continued practice with sentence formation and question structures will be beneficial. Encouragement in storytelling activities will also help build her confidence and fluency.

Final comment

Camille has demonstrated a positive and enthusiastic approach to her learning this term. Her ability to recall vocabulary and participate in group activities highlights her engagement and motivation. While she occasionally requires reminders to maintain focus, her overall behavior and cooperation are commendable.
